extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutions applying for Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program (PRCRP) funding; stakeholders (Service members, Veterans), program reviewers, and funders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level criteria for aligning cancer research proposals with the Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program: its vision, mission, topic-area eligibility, and funding priorities (innovation, translational spectrum, and military-relevance). Useful for prospective applicants preparing applications and institutional grant support staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision – Eliminate the burden of cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-level aspirational goal: funded research should contribute toward eliminating cancer burden. No scoring details provided on the page; serves as overarching aim to guide topic selection and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission (priority areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission – To successfully promote high-impact research in cancer prevention, detection, treatment, quality of life, and survivorship for Service Members, their families, Veterans, and the American public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should align with mission by proposing high-impact work addressing prevention, detection, treatment, quality of life, or survivorship, and should consider relevance to Service members, Veterans, families, or the broader U.S. public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research impact and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Fiscal Year 2009 (FY09), the Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program (PRCRP) has funded innovative basic, applied, translational, and clinical cancer research to support Service members, Veterans, their families, and the American public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to innovative projects across the research spectrum (basic → applied → translational → clinical). Proposals should emphasize innovation and potential for high impact; the program explicitly funds work across these research types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-spectrum/translational emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: To accomplish this, the PRCRP invests in the full spectrum of cancer research from discovery to clinical application, focusing on funding gaps in the research landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that fill identified funding gaps and move discoveries toward clinical application are consistent with program aims. Applicants should highlight translational potential and where the project fits within the discovery-to-clinic continuum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of military readiness / relevance to Service members
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of the PRCRP is to protect and sustain military readiness by promoting high-impact research for cancer prevention, detection, treatment, and survivorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should, when possible, articulate how the proposed research relates to protecting or sustaining military readiness or addresses cancer risks associated with military service (e.g., exposures during duty/deployments). Relevance to the military population is an explicit program consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-area eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRCRP is a multi-topic research program and has supported over 1100 awards under 33 congressionally-directed topic areas including specific cancer types, groups of cancers, and cancer research areas such as immunology. A list of the current PRCRP topic areas is below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered by the program, proposed work should fall within one of the PRCRP's current topic areas (the page lists topics such as Bladder Cancer, Blood Cancers, Brain Cancer, Colorectal Cancer, etc.). Applicants must select an applicable topic area and justify alignment with that topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority toward cancers and topics with demonstrated burden among Service members
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRCRP topic areas represent 72% of cancer-related medical encounters by active-duty Service Members and their family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program topic selection is informed by burden-of-disease data for Service members and families. Proposals addressing topics with higher burden in the military population may be especially relevant; applicants should note any burden data or military-specific rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic and peer review structure (two-tiered review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two Tiered Review Process (referenced in site navigation and program pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program uses programmatic panels and peer review participants (e.g., Programmatic Panels, Peer Review Participants listed for FY25/FY26). Applicants should expect a structured peer-review process (technical peer review and programmatic review) — align application presentation to both scientific rigor and programmatic impact criteria. The page lists programmatic panels and peer review participant lists but does not provide detailed review criteria on this page.
